title: AWS Transit Gateway Attachment Health

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay sample `aws:config:notification` events with `( resourceType="AWS::EC2::TransitGatewayAttachment" OR (sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch" namespace="AWS/TransitGateway" metric_name="BytesIn"))` into `index=aws`. Confirm UC-4.1.58 returns >=1 row and the alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `aws:config:notification` traffic without `( resourceType="AWS::EC2::TransitGatewayAttachment" OR (sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch" namespace="AWS/TransitGateway" metric_name="BytesIn"))`. Confirm UC-4.1.58 returns zero rows and the alert does not fire.

dataSources: `index=aws` sourcetype=`aws:config:notification` collected via `Splunk_TA_aws`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=aws sourcetype="aws:config:notification" ( resourceType="AWS::EC2::TransitGatewayAttachment" OR (sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch" namespace="AWS/TransitGateway" metric_name="BytesIn"))
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.58_aws_transit_gateway_atta_58"
| sort -_time
description: UC-4.1.58 — AWS Transit Gateway Attachment Health: queries AWS `aws:config:notification` for search criteria `( resourceType="AWS::EC2::TransitGatewayAttachment" OR (sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch" namesp` and returns actor, resource, and region context for availability review and change validation.
value: On AWS, detecting 'AWS Transit Gateway Attachment Health' early shortens cloud incident response and produces defensible audit evidence for identity and change-management controls. UC-4.1.58 drives high-priority availability alerting before customer-impacting drift.

detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_aws` with the modular input for `aws:config:notification`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.1.78.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Enable AWS Config for TGW attachments to track state changes. Ingest TGW flow logs to S3 and forward to Splunk for traffic analysis. Collect CloudWatch TGW metrics (BytesIn, BytesOut) per attachment. Alert when attachment state is not available or traffic drops to zero unexpectedly. Correlate with route table propagation events. Use for hybrid connectivity and SD-WAN monitoring.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:config:notification" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:config:notification" ( resourceType="AWS::EC2::TransitGatewayAttachment" OR (sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch" namespace="AWS/TransitGateway" metric_name="BytesIn"))
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.58_aws_transit_gateway_atta_58"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:config:notification` in `index=aws` to detect aws transit gateway attachment health. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_1_58_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Table (attachment, state, traffic), Status grid (attachment health), Line chart (bytes in/out by attachment)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_aws` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of aws transit gateway attachment health so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
